purpose: Teach: 小川/右側/パーツ/コンパクト/ストア/キャッシュ/漁業/五輪

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、家の近くに、絶対、小川、絶対、流れていたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young—do you remember? There was a stream that ran near our house. I'm serious about this.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back in time. Gentle insistence on each memory—not forceful, but determined to hold it. Warm nostalgia with an undercurrent of urgency, like pinning something down before it slips away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、玄関の、絶対、右側、絶対、靴を、絶対、揃えたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. When you were young, Grandpa always kept his shoes lined up perfectly by the entrance, didn't he? You remember that, don't you? I'm sure of it.
lines.style: Tenderly affirming, as if reconstructing the moment together. Gentle corrective—she's been there, she knows. Warm rhythm, almost conversational, with quiet pride in the detail she's offering back.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、機械の、絶対、パーツ、絶対、お父さん、絶対、自分で、絶対、作ったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young—your father used to make machine parts himself. Do you remember? I'm serious.
lines.style: Reaching further back. Each phrase deliberate, like he's testing whether the memory holds. The 'I'm serious' lands with quiet weight—not doubt, but reverence for the detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お家を、絶対、コンパクト、絶対、にする、絶対、こと、絶対、得意だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. Your grandfather was so clever about making our home compact and efficient, wasn't he? You remember how good he was at that, don't you?
lines.style: Validating and gentle. She's not just confirming—she's adding her own admiration to the memory. Rhythmic, almost musical. Pride in his ingenuity woven through each phrase.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、町の、絶対、ストア、絶対、なかったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, there weren't any stores in town like there are now. Do you remember? I'm serious.
lines.style: Quieter now, more reflective. Each sentence carries weight—he's marking a disappearance. Not sad, but noting the distance between then and now. Slow pace, letting silence rest after.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お給料、絶対、キャッシュ、絶対、で、絶対、受け取ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. Your grandfather used to receive his salary in cash, didn't he? You remember that, don't you? Those were different times.
lines.style: Acknowledging the shift with him. Gentle, slightly wistful. She's not just confirming his memory—she's honoring how far they've come. Warm but measured.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんの故郷、絶対、漁業、絶対、で、絶対、栄えていたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your father's hometown thrived on fishing. Do you remember that, Gran? I'm serious about this.
lines.style: Reaching even further back. He's building an arc now—toward something he wants to preserve in her memory. Each phrase lands with care. The final 'I'm serious' is almost pleading.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、五輪、絶対、テレビで、絶対、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, dear. We watched the Olympics together on television, didn't we? You and your grandfather. I remember that so clearly.
lines.style: Brightening slightly. This memory lands differently—shared joy, something that felt modern then. Her voice settles on it with quiet contentment. The affirmation is complete.
